sents.t: One rainy Monday in April, I was driving to work when I heard a loud noise: bump, bump, bump.
I pulled over to the side of the road and got out.
My front tire was completely flat!
I had a spare tire in the trunk, but I didn’t know how to change it.
While I was waiting in the rain, a police officer stopped.
“Are you OK? You should turn on your hazard lights,” she said.
When Carlos arrived, he showed me how to use the jack.
We changed the tire together, and my jeans got very muddy.
“The spare is only for emergencies,” Carlos said.
“Take the car to Gus’s Garage after work.”
That evening, the mechanic, Gus, found a nail in the old tire.
“I can’t fix this one. You’ll need a new tire,” he said.
“And your brakes are a little old. You should replace them soon.”
The new tire cost a hundred and twenty dollars.
Owning a car is more expensive than I thought!

comp.q: What was wrong with the car?
What did the police officer tell Sam?
o: to turn on his hazard lights
comp.fa: افسر پلیس به سام چه گفت؟

comp.q: What was in the old tire?
What else did the mechanic say?
o: Sam should replace the brakes soon.
